newsitem.title: GREECE: ATHLETICS-COLD WEATHER LOVER KORZENIOWSKI PROSPERS IN HEAT.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-COLD WEATHER LOVER KORZENIOWSKI PROSPERS IN HEAT.

text.p: Poland's Robert Korzeniowski, an avowed lover of a chilly climate, added the world 50 kms title to his Olympic gold on Thursday in sweltering Athenian heat.
The winner of the Atlanta Olympic title moved to northern France to train because the conditions were similar to his native country.
Nevertheless on Thursday he showed himself to be a fierce competitor in the temperatures which soared into the late thirties despite a seven a.m. start.

"It's really weird," Korzeniowski said. "I don't like the heat and I don't train in hot conditions but I concentrated well and I'm starting to get used to it now that nearly every championship is held in the heat."
The weather conditions meant that his winning time of three hours 44 minutes 46 seconds was relatively modest.
He and 1997 World Cup winner Jesus Garcia, from Spain, were out on their own after 34 kilometres then duelled for another 10 kms before Korzeniowski made his decisive surge.
Garcia, who had tried to effect his own break away in the eraly stages of the race, did not give up the fight until the final few hundred metres but had to settle for the silver medal in 3:44:59.
The leaders finished more than three-and-a-half minutes ahead of Mexico's Miguel Rodriguez, who walked a superb second half to take the bronze medal in 3:48:30.
Rodriguez was lying ninth at the halfway mark, well adrift of the leading pack, but picked off walkers one-by-one over the final 20 kilometres.

"I have trained specifically for the heat and I knew some of the good walkers like the Russians are really cold weather people," Rodriguez said. "I thought I could beat everyone in the leading pack except for Garcia and Korzeniowski, so I suppose I was always racing for the bronze medal."
Korzeniowski was delighted with his second major honour after his Olympic title, " It will be nice to have the two gold medals side-by-side."
However he criticised the Athens organisers for stationing drinks stations every two kms.
"It caused a lot of problems for the walkers. In Atlanta they had them every 600 to 800 metres," Koarseniowski said.
